title: Drone Parts Assembly with Undo/Redo
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js that implements a drone parts assembly configurator with undo/redo functionality. Load the 'soldier.glb' model using GLTFLoader from a CDN (https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/) as a decorative operator figure standing beside the assembly area.

SCENE SETUP:
- Set up a Three.js scene with a perspective camera at position (0, 5, 10) looking at the origin.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.5) and a directional light at (5, 10, 5) with intensity 1.0.
- Add a ground plane (20x20, gray color #888888) at y=0.
- Load 'soldier.glb' using GLTFLoader and place it at position (-5, 0, 0) scaled to 2.0. This is the drone operator figure.

DRONE PARTS (create these as simple Three.js geometries):
1. FRAME: A flat box (2x0.2x2, color #333333) representing the drone body. Starts at position (5, 0.5, 3) in the parts tray area.
2. MOTOR_FL (Front-Left Motor): A cylinder (radius 0.15, height 0.4, color #FF4444) starting at (4, 0.5, 5).
3. MOTOR_FR (Front-Right Motor): A cylinder (radius 0.15, height 0.4, color #FF4444) starting at (6, 0.5, 5).
4. MOTOR_BL (Back-Left Motor): A cylinder (radius 0.15, height 0.4, color #4444FF) starting at (4, 0.5, 6).
5. MOTOR_BR (Back-Right Motor): A cylinder (radius 0.15, height 0.4, color #4444FF) starting at (6, 0.5, 6).
6. BATTERY: A box (0.6x0.3x0.4, color #00CC00) starting at (5, 0.5, 7).
7. CAMERA_MODULE: A small sphere (radius 0.2, color #FFAA00) starting at (5, 0.5, 8).

ASSEMBLY POSITIONS (where parts snap to when assembled onto the frame at origin):
- FRAME assembles to: (0, 2, 0)
- MOTOR_FL: (-0.8, 2.3, -0.8)
- MOTOR_FR: (0.8, 2.3, -0.8)
- MOTOR_BL: (-0.8, 2.3, 0.8)
- MOTOR_BR: (0.8, 2.3, 0.8)
- BATTERY: (0, 1.85, 0)
- CAMERA_MODULE: (0, 1.6, -0.5)

ASSEMBLY RULES:
- Parts must be assembled in a valid order: FRAME must be placed first. Motors can be placed in any order but only after FRAME. BATTERY requires FRAME. CAMERA_MODULE requires FRAME and BATTERY.
- Parts that cannot be placed yet should show a red flash if the user tries.

UI ELEMENTS:
- Create an HTML overlay panel on the left side with:
  - Title 'Drone Assembly' as an h2
  - A parts list showing each part name and its status: 'In Tray' / 'Assembled'
  - An 'Assemble Next' button (id='btn-assemble') that assembles the next valid part in order: FRAME -> MOTOR_FL -> MOTOR_FR -> MOTOR_BL -> MOTOR_BR -> BATTERY -> CAMERA_MODULE
  - An 'Undo' button (id='btn-undo') that reverses the last assembly action
  - A 'Redo' button (id='btn-redo') that re-applies an undone action
  - A 'Reset All' button (id='btn-reset') that returns all parts to their tray positions
  - A progress bar (id='progress-bar') showing assembly completion percentage (0% to 100%)
  - Assembly count display (id='assembly-count') showing 'X / 7 parts assembled'

ANIMATION:
- When a part is assembled, animate it smoothly (over 0.5 seconds) from its tray position to its assembly position using lerp or tween.
- When undone, animate it back to its tray position.

STATE MANAGEMENT:
- Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
  - partsAssembled: number (0-7, count of assembled parts)
  - assemblyOrder: array of part name strings in the order they were assembled
  - undoStackSize: number (how many actions can be undone)
  - redoStackSize: number (how many actions can be redone)
  - progressPercent: number (0-100, rounded to nearest integer)
  - frameAssembled: boolean
  - allMotorsAssembled: boolean (true when all 4 motors placed)
  - batteryAssembled: boolean
  - cameraAssembled: boolean
  - droneComplete: boolean (true when all 7 parts assembled)
  - soldierLoaded: boolean (true when soldier.glb finishes loading)
  - partPositions: object mapping part names to {x, y, z} current positions

Update window.__3D_STATE__ after every action (assemble, undo, redo, reset).

KEYBOARD SHORTCUTS:
- Press 'N' to assemble next part (same as clicking Assemble Next)
- Press 'Z' to undo
- Press 'Y' to redo
- Press 'R' to reset all

ENSURE:
- OrbitControls for camera rotation
- Responsive layout
- No NaN values in any state fields
- Animation loop with requestAnimationFrame
physics_constraints: Parts must snap to exact assembly positions. Parts animate smoothly (lerp) between tray and assembly positions. Assembly order constraints must be enforced (frame first, motors/battery require frame, camera requires frame+battery). Undo/redo stacks must maintain consistency.
